Looking at this again more carefully.

The statute at §152(c)(2) states: "an individual bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in this paragraph if such individual is - (A) a child of the taxpayer or a descendant of such a child, or (B) a brother, sister, stepbrother, or stepsister..."

This defines when someone (the "individual") bears a relationship to the "taxpayer" (the person claiming the exemption). 

For a parent-child relationship where Alice is the mother and Bob is her son:
- Bob (the son) bears a relationship to Alice (the taxpayer) ✓ under 152(c)(2)(A)
- Alice (the mother) does NOT bear a relationship to Bob under 152(c)(2) because she is a parent, not a child

Since a parent is not a "child of the taxpayer" as required by 152(c)(2)(A), the claim that "Alice bears a relationship to Bob under section 152(c)(2)" is FALSE. Parent-child relationships are covered under 152(d)(2)(C) for qualifying relatives, not under 152(c)(2) for qualifying children.

Answer: Contradiction
